5G Drive-Test KPI Analyzer

Drive-test dashboard: 16 drives in Cork

27,591 samples from a phone downloading while driving, 2019-12-14 to 2020-02-27. One operator, 5G NSA with LTE and 3G fallback.

Coverage and signal quality

How strong and how clean the signal was. On 5G rows the phone reports the LTE anchor cell (5G NSA), so these values compare the anchor layer with plain LTE.

Throughput

Downlink throughput while the phone was downloading. The axis is logarithmic: each step to the right is ten times faster.

Cell changes

The log shows when the serving cell changes. That can be a handover, a reselection or a re-establishment; the log cannot tell them apart.

Ping-pong: does it belong to particular borders?

A rule is good when it acts on many ping-pong round trips and on few normal changes. Knowing that a border had a round trip in another drive acts on 76% of the round trips and on 40% of the normal changes. A 3 dB signal margin acts on 68% and 55%. So in this log the border says more than the signal gain. But 79 of the 148 round trips last 2 seconds or less and may be effects of the logger. Without them no difference can be shown. The border list shows where to look first; it is not a tuning recommendation.

Map

All drives in 100 m road bins. Switch layers in the top right corner. A ring marks a weak spot that was seen in at least two drives.

Throughput prediction

Three models predict the throughput of the next 10 seconds. They are tested on drives they never saw. Radio KPIs alone explain little; location and recent history explain much more.

The drives

Each drive has its own report with the same layout.

Data: D. Raca, D. Leahy, C. J. Sreenan and J. J. Quinlan, "Beyond Throughput, The Next Generation: a 5G Dataset with Channel and Context Metrics", ACM MMSys 2020 (uccmisl/5Gdataset, GPL-3.0). Download-while-driving logs from Cork, Ireland, recorded with G-NetTrack Pro.

Every number on this page is computed from the raw logs by this code.

The log is application-level: it shows serving-cell changes, not the handover signalling. A change can be a handover, a reselection or a re-establishment.

On 5G rows the radio values most likely describe the LTE anchor cell (5G NSA). That is an inference from the data; the log does not state it.
